content: 轻资产酒店集团扩张，争取合同的资金该投向哪里？
轻资产酒店集团扩张时，争取合同的下一笔资金，应按可核实的丢单主因，在逐店支持与系统、业主支持能力之间选择，再用合同质量和集团留下的收费现金检验。签约或开业客房增加，只回答了规模问题。
这里比较的是同一集团有权自主决定、尚未承诺的增量资源。受限资金、已经签下的支持义务和维持现有合同所必需的投入，先留在各自用途里。不能为了比较两个方案，把原本无权挪用的钱重新变成预算。
一、酒店集团扩张，究竟输在哪类项目上？
追加获约资金前，发展与财务高管应先共同复核赢单和丢单。只把原因写成价格不够优惠，无法判断缺的是一笔项目资金，还是集团长期没有兑现的能力。
可以从已有项目记录中，选取同市场、相近品牌定位和开发阶段的赢输项目，核对业主反馈、报价版本、融资条件及最终选择。发展团队解释商业背景，财务核对支持条件有没有在谈判中变化；把未经业主或文件印证的推测单列，不替竞争对手编造补贴金额。
项目本身合格，业主只是缺少一段有明确用途和来源安排的资金，与业主反复质疑开业支持、系统交付或结算服务，是不同障碍。前一种需要审查有限支持能否促成可履行合同；后一种才值得研究共享能力是否存在缺口。项目定位、回报诉求或物业条件根本不匹配时，给钱和做系统都可能无效。
还要保留退出谈判的项目，避免只研究最后成功签下的酒店。支持后签约，也可能来自市场转暖、融资落实或商务条款变化。若没有可比项目和谈判过程证据，就先验证丢单解释，不把时间先后写成获约投入的效果。
二、合同现金、技术受偿与担保，为什么必须分开？
万豪2026年第三季度报告把合同取得现金列在经营活动，把资本及技术支出列在投资活动。其2025年会计政策又分别列示合同取得成本的资产、摊销和现金流影响。资产余额或摊销，不能代替本期支付。
同一季度报告说明，全球技术系统转型有高于常规水平的预期投入，其中绝大部分预计随时间获得偿付。这一限定针对技术转型，不能扩成所有技术支出已经获偿，更不能把成本受偿直接算成新增利润。集团应同时看毛付款、可执行的受偿安排、到账时间和最终净负担；长期可收回，也可能需要先垫资。
担保另列。万豪2025年承诺及或有事项披露，部分担保主要用于取得长期特许经营和管理合同；2026年第三季度报告仍列有须待酒店开业等事件才生效的保证。尚未触发付款的义务，仍可能占用未来资源。最大潜在拨付、账面负债、预期损失与实付现金，各自回答不同问题，不应相加充作投入总额。
这些公开披露能帮助拆清支出性质，不能证明转换增长推高了获约成本，也没有替其他集团排出资金投向。尤其不能拿当期开业客房去除合同取得现金：付款与开业未必来自同一批合同，合同类型和期间也可能不同。
三、下一笔资源怎样形成一项可以批准的提案？
董事会需要看到的是障碍如何被解除、集团因此取得什么，以及何时停止追加。发展负责人可与财务负责人把候选项目或能力提案放入下面这张表，先用现有记录核实，再提交有条件的资金申请。

待核实的丢单障碍	拟追加的资源	集团要取得的结果	追加或停止的依据
合格项目存在可补救的融资缺口	有上限、按条件支付的逐店支持	可履行的合同、按约收费，以及扣清支持和持续服务投入后的现金结果	融资条件落实才付款，条件落空重审
相近项目反复质疑同一项服务能力	针对该缺口的系统或业主支持投入	能力被采用，目标合同的收费和留存改善	未解决原障碍或持续成本失控则停止扩围
业主诉求与品牌、项目条件不匹配	调整目标项目或暂缓承诺	避免取得需长期额外补贴的合同	适配性未改变，不靠继续加钱推进
丢单归因仍主要依赖内部推测	先补谈判及项目证据	把真实障碍与销售解释分开	证据足够后再审资金，不先设两边比例
表中是本文建议的提案框架，并非公司的现行制度或统一行业标准。逐店支持要写清付款触发、支持上限、收费让步、追回或终止条件及其可执行性；不能只报一次性付款，省略未来减免费用和继续追加的可能。
共享能力提案则应说明服务哪些合同、由谁使用、谁承担持续运行和升级费用。如果价值只能归到整个集团，无法指出它将改变哪类业主的选择，就还不足以批准全面建设。两类提案都可以被否决，也可能需要先补一项小范围验证。
四、集团最终留下多少收费现金，怎样核清？
合同质量要从签约后继续追到履行。项目能否按约开业、收费权能否执行、业主能否支付，以及合同是否需要不断增加支持，都会改变集团实际得到的东西。
本次决策先约定比较的合同组和观察期间，再从收费实收中扣除为取得、履行和维持这些合同增加的现金支持、实际支付的服务费用及相应税费，观察集团留下的现金。这是管理比较口径，不是财报净收费收入；未来收支预测与已收已付分开，再结合各自合同期限审查，不能把延后付款当成节约。
技术受偿、追回款与对应支出，应按同一项目或合同组列明金额和实际收付日期。已用到账受偿抵减对应支出的，不再另加一次回款。共享系统的初建、维护、升级和业主支持现金支出单列，说明受益范围及归属依据；不能把原本就要发生的总部支出重复扣给新合同。
对预计受偿的投入，财务还要测算到账延迟或对方违约时的垫资峰值。担保敞口、可能触发的付款与本期实际付款分列；实际付款纳入所属合同组的现金支出，未触发风险另做情景审查，不混入当期已付现金，也不因尚未付款就忽略未来资金占用。合同留存也要与收费条件一起看：靠反复减免费用换来的延续，未必保住了原先的合同价值。
五、怎样验证，而不等整个系统建完再复盘？
由首席执行官明确试验范围和授权，发展、财务及相关能力负责人共同选定下一组可比项目。董事会按金额和风险权限批准分阶段投入，不预设逐店支持与共享建设的固定比例。
逐店支持从一组条件可核的项目开始，付款与约定里程碑相连。能力建设则先交付能针对原丢单问题使用的一段服务，不把完整平台上线当作首个检验点。批准时一并确定记录起点、下一次检查日期和后续检查所需的合同事件；开发周期较长，先查条件是否落实，不能提前宣布留存或现金回收已经改善。
复盘时保留同批未获支持、尚未使用新能力的可比项目，并记录地区需求、业主融资和商务条款变化。对照只能帮助识别解释，不能消除项目选择偏差。实际收费、合同履行和持续服务支出未达到原假设时，应重新审查归因和承诺，不能拿签约数增加替代结果。
六、哪些反证会改变资金投向？
以下是条件推演，不是客户案例。若系统已能满足目标业主，重复丢单主要来自业主融资，那么共享能力优先的提议应被推翻；但项目缺口没有可行补救，逐店给钱也不应继续。
反过来，若有限支持只能换来更低费率和后续加码，合同履行、净收费现金及留存仍不成立，就应收缩这类获约方式。若服务能力确有不足，却没有足够目标合同采用，或维护支出持续超出假设，也应停止扩围。需要停止的是新增承诺；已经承担的合同义务仍须依法依约处理。
下一次发展投资会，可以先从一组赢输项目带来的证据出发，决定要解除哪个障碍，再审资金提案。集团真正要买到的，是能够履行、持续收费并负担得起服务的合同关系。
业主一侧的选择权，可参阅《品牌合同快到期，续约、换牌还是独立经营？酒店业主该怎样决策？》。迈创兄弟C&T可协助梳理获约条件与后续收费、支持投入之间的联系。

contentEn: As Asset-Light Hotel Groups Expand, Where Should They Allocate Funds to Win Contracts?

As an asset-light hotel group expands, its next allocation of funds to win contracts should follow the verifiable main reasons for lost deals. It should choose between hotel-specific support and investment in systems and owner-support capabilities, then test the decision against contract quality and the cash it retains from fees. More rooms signed or opened answers only the question of scale.

The comparison here concerns uncommitted incremental resources that the same group has discretion to allocate. Restricted funds, support obligations already contracted, and spending necessary to maintain existing contracts must first remain assigned to their respective purposes. Comparing two options does not turn money the group has no authority to reallocate into an available budget.
I. Which kinds of projects is the hotel group losing?

Before allocating more funds to secure contracts, development and finance executives should jointly review wins and losses. Simply recording the reason as insufficiently attractive pricing does not establish whether the missing element is project funding or a capability the group has long failed to deliver.

Existing project records can be used to select wins and losses in the same market, with similar brand positioning and development stages, and check owner feedback, versions of offers, financing terms and final decisions. The development team explains the commercial context, while finance checks whether support terms changed during negotiations. Set aside conjecture not corroborated by owners or documents, and do not invent competitors' subsidy amounts.

An eligible project whose owner only needs funding for a defined purpose with an identified funding arrangement presents a different obstacle from owners repeatedly questioning opening support, systems delivery or settlement services. The first calls for assessing whether limited support can secure a contract that can be fulfilled; the second warrants investigating a gap in shared capabilities. Where project positioning, return expectations or property conditions are fundamentally mismatched, neither money nor systems may help.

Include projects where negotiations were abandoned, rather than studying only hotels that eventually signed. A signing after support was provided could also reflect a market recovery, financing secured or changes in commercial terms. Without comparable projects and evidence from the negotiations, first test the explanation for the loss; do not treat the sequence of events as proof that spending to win the contract worked.
II. Why must cash payments to obtain contracts, technology reimbursements and guarantees be kept separate?

Marriott International's 2026 third-quarter report classifies cash payments to obtain contracts within operating activities and capital and technology expenditures within investing activities. Its 2025 accounting policies separately present the assets, amortization and cash flow effects of costs to obtain contracts. An asset balance or amortization cannot substitute for payments made in the current period.

The same quarterly report describes higher-than-normal expected spending on the transformation of its global technology systems, the vast majority of which is expected to be reimbursed over time. This qualification concerns the technology transformation. It does not mean that all technology spending has already been reimbursed, nor can cost reimbursements simply be counted as additional profit. A group should examine gross payments, enforceable reimbursement arrangements, when cash will arrive and the ultimate net cost together. Even spending recoverable over the long term may require funding upfront.

Keep guarantees separate. Marriott's 2025 commitments and contingencies disclosures state that some guarantees are primarily used to obtain long-term franchise and management contracts. Its 2026 third-quarter report still lists guarantees that do not become effective until events such as a hotel's opening. Obligations that have not yet triggered a payment may still absorb future resources. Maximum potential future funding, recorded liabilities, expected losses and actual cash paid answer different questions; they should not be added together as a total investment figure.

These public disclosures help distinguish the nature of spending. They do not establish that growth in hotel conversions has driven up the cost of winning contracts, nor do they determine funding priorities for other groups. In particular, do not divide cash payments to obtain contracts by rooms opened in the current period: the payments and openings may not relate to the same contracts, and contract types and periods may also differ.
III. What would make the next funding proposal ready for approval?

The board needs to see how the obstacle will be removed, what the group will gain, and when to stop adding resources. The heads of development and finance can use the table below for candidate projects or capability proposals, verify them against existing records, then submit conditional funding requests.

Lost-deal obstacle to verify	Additional resources proposed	Outcome the group needs	Basis for adding support or stopping
An eligible project has a financing gap that can be remedied	Capped, conditional hotel-specific support	A contract that can be fulfilled, fees collected as agreed, and the cash outcome after deducting support and ongoing service spending	Pay only when financing conditions are met; reassess if they fall through
Similar projects repeatedly question the same service capability	Systems or owner-support spending targeted at that gap	The capability is adopted, and fee outcomes and retention improve for the target contracts	Stop expanding the initiative if the original obstacle remains unresolved or ongoing costs get out of control
Owner expectations do not fit the brand or project conditions	Adjust target projects or defer commitments	Avoid contracts requiring long-term additional subsidies	Do not keep adding money to move negotiations forward if the fit has not changed
The explanation for lost deals still relies mainly on internal conjecture	First obtain more evidence from negotiations and projects	Separate real obstacles from sales explanations	Review funding once the evidence is sufficient, rather than setting a ratio between the two options first

The table is this article's proposed framework, not an existing company policy or a uniform industry standard. Hotel-specific support must specify payment triggers, support caps, fee concessions, clawback or termination conditions and their enforceability. Do not report only the one-time payment while omitting future fee reductions or waivers and the possibility of further support.

A shared-capability proposal should explain which contracts it serves, who will use it, and who bears ongoing operating and upgrade costs. If its value can only be attributed to the group as a whole, with no indication of which owners' choices it will change, that is not yet enough to approve a full rollout. Either type of proposal can be rejected, and either may first need a limited test.
IV. How can the group establish how much cash it ultimately retains from fees?

Track contract quality beyond signing through to performance. Whether a project can open as agreed, fee rights are enforceable, the owner can pay, and the contract needs ever more support all change what the group actually receives.

For this decision, first agree on the group of contracts and observation period to compare. Then deduct from fees actually collected the additional cash support, actual payments for services, and corresponding taxes and charges paid to obtain, fulfill and maintain those contracts, and examine the cash the group retains. This is a management comparison measure, not net fee revenue reported in financial statements. Keep forecasts of future receipts and payments separate from cash already received and paid, and review them in light of the respective contract terms. Deferred payment is not a saving.

List technology reimbursements, clawbacks and the corresponding spending by the same project or group of contracts, specifying amounts and actual receipt and payment dates. Once reimbursement received has been netted against the corresponding spending, do not add it again as another cash receipt. Show cash spending on the initial build, maintenance and upgrades of shared systems and on owner support separately, explaining who benefits and the basis for attribution. Do not deduct headquarters spending that would have occurred anyway from new contracts a second time.

For spending expected to be reimbursed, finance should also calculate the peak funding required if receipts are delayed or the counterparty defaults. Show guarantee exposure, payments that might be triggered and actual payments in the current period separately. Include actual payments in the cash spending of the relevant group of contracts. Review risks not yet triggered in separate scenarios: do not mix them with cash paid in the current period, or ignore their future funding demands because no payment has yet been made. Assess contract retention alongside fee terms; an extension obtained through repeated fee reductions or waivers may not preserve the original contract value.
V. How can the group test the decision without waiting for the entire system to be built?

The chief executive officer should define the test's scope and delegated authority, while development, finance and the relevant capability leads jointly select the next group of comparable projects. The board approves phased spending within the applicable amount and risk authorities, without setting a fixed ratio between hotel-specific support and shared-capability development in advance.

Begin hotel-specific support with a group of projects whose conditions can be verified, linking payments to agreed milestones. For capability development, first deliver a usable part of the service that addresses the original reason for lost deals; do not make the launch of a complete platform the first test point. At approval, also establish the starting point for records, the next review date and the contract events needed for subsequent reviews. Where development cycles are long, first check whether conditions have been met; do not announce improved retention or cash recovery prematurely.

In the review, retain comparable projects from the same group that received no support or have not yet used the new capability, and record changes in regional demand, owner financing and commercial terms. Comparisons can help identify explanations, but cannot eliminate project selection bias. If actual fees, performance under contracts and ongoing service spending fall short of the original assumptions, reassess attribution and commitments; more contracts signed cannot substitute for results.
VI. What counterevidence would change the allocation of funds?

The following are conditional scenarios, not client cases. If the systems already meet target owners' needs and repeated losses are mainly due to owner financing, a proposal to prioritize shared capabilities should be overturned. But if the project's funding gap has no viable remedy, hotel-specific funding should not continue either.

Conversely, if limited support buys only lower fee rates and demands for further support, while performance under contracts, net cash from fees and retention still do not hold up, scale back this approach to winning contracts. If service capability is genuinely lacking but too few target contracts will use it, or maintenance spending keeps exceeding assumptions, stop expanding the initiative as well. It is new commitments that need to stop; contractual obligations already assumed must still be handled in accordance with the law and the contracts.

At the next development investment meeting, start with evidence from a group of wins and losses, decide which obstacle needs to be removed, then review the funding proposal. What the group really needs to secure is a contractual relationship it can fulfill, collect fees from on an ongoing basis, and afford to service.

For the owner's side of the decision, see When a Brand Contract Is Near Expiry, How Should a Hotel Owner Decide Among Renewal, Reflagging and Independent Operation? MarvelBros C&T can help map the links between the terms for winning contracts, subsequent fee collections and support spending.
